solution:
Separate variables: $\dfrac{dy}{y(2-y)}=dx$.
Partial fractions: $\dfrac{1}{y(2-y)}=\tfrac12\left(\dfrac1y+\dfrac1{2-y}\right)$.
Integrating:
$$\tfrac12\bigl(\ln|y|-\ln|2-y|\bigr)=x+C\quad\Rightarrow\quad \ln\left|\frac{y}{2-y}\right|=2x+C'.$$
At $x=0$, $y=1$: $\ln(1)=0=C'$. So $\ln\dfrac{y}{2-y}=2x$, giving $\dfrac{y}{2-y}=e^{2x}$.
Hence $y=(2-y)e^{2x}$, so $y(1+e^{2x})=2e^{2x}$ and
$$y=\frac{2e^{2x}}{1+e^{2x}}.$$
